<reason>Side B (PRO) built the stronger path to victory by establishing that rudimentary learning marks a functional threshold warranting precautionary oversight under the Three Rs, exposing the critical timing gap in Side A's position (which would require waiting for anatomical structures like brainstems that dish-bound organoids may never develop), and effectively countering the "category error" claim by identifying the welfare interest as preventing central neural distress from aversive stimulation. Side B's Rebuttal 2 decisively exposed the contradiction in Side A's stance on monitoring neural integration markers while refusing to trigger review at the learning stage. While Side A mounted a strong defense of the computation-consciousness distinction and biological prerequisites for suffering, it failed to neutralize the precautionary principle or demonstrate that animal review frameworks are logically incoherent rather than merely adaptable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 (B4.1-B4.4), particularly the exposure of the contradiction in Side A's position regarding monitoring for neural integration markers versus denying current welfare risk, and the functional application of the Three Rs to prevent central neural distress from chronic aversive stimulation.</best_rebuttal>
